title: You Lead a Galactic House
textBlocks:
Welcome to Voidfall -- a space civilization game of exploration, expansion, exploitation, and extermination (the classic 4X formula) wrapped in a tight euro-game framework.

You are the leader of a Galactic House, one of the great powers in a galaxy under siege. An existential threat called the {{glossary:voidborn|Voidborn}} has been consuming entire star systems, leaving nothing but darkness and {{glossary:corruption|Corruption}} in its wake. Your mission is twofold: push back the Voidborn and build a thriving interstellar empire.

Voidfall is designed by Nigel Buckle and David Turczi, published by Mindclash Games in 2023. It supports 1-4 players and plays in roughly 2 to 4 hours depending on player count. This is a heavy game (complexity 4.6 out of 5), but the rules are logical and interconnected -- once the core systems click, everything flows naturally.

callouts.content: Do not worry about memorizing everything at once. This teaching flow builds understanding layer by layer. Each new concept connects to what you already know.

title: Your Goal: Influence
textBlocks: The victory currency of Voidfall is {{glossary:influence|Influence}}. Everything you do -- conquering {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s, completing objectives, advancing your civilization, building an efficient economy -- ultimately serves the goal of accumulating Influence.

In competitive mode (2-4 players): The player with the most Influence at the end of the game wins. If tied, the player with fewer {{glossary:corruption|Corruption}} markers on their House mat and sectors wins.

In cooperative/solo mode: All players must individually exceed the {{glossary:voidborn|Voidborn}}'s collective Influence total. The Voidborn's score is calculated at end of game based on how much destruction it caused -- every Catastrophe, Corruption marker, and unresolved Crisis adds to its total.

callouts.content: Influence is tracked on your personal Influence board with dials. Many different game actions generate or cost Influence, so keep an eye on your total throughout the game.

title: Three Ways to Play
rawHtml:
Welcome to Voidfall

Three Ways to Play

Voidfall offers three distinct game modes. Tap each to learn more.

1 Competitive (2-4 players)

Players compete for Influence. You fight the Voidborn while also vying against each other for territory and objectives. The player with the most Influence at the end wins.

2 Cooperative (2-4 players)

Players work together against the Voidborn. Additional Crisis mechanics create ongoing threats. All players must individually exceed the Voidborn's collective Influence total to win. Difficulty levels set the Voidborn's base score at 60, 100, or 140.

3 Solo (1 player)

You face the Voidborn alone using the same cooperative rules and Crisis mechanics. The Voidborn's base Influence starts at 60 (easy), 100 (medium), or 140 (hard). You must exceed its total to win.

title: Exactly Three Cycles
textBlocks:
Voidfall lasts exactly 3 Cycles. There is no way to shorten or extend the game. Each Cycle is divided into three phases:

  1. Preparation Phase -- Set up for the Cycle (reveal {{glossary:galactic_event|Galactic Event}}, determine turn order, resolve event instructions)
  2. Focus Phase -- The main gameplay. Multiple rounds where players take turns playing {{glossary:focus_card|Focus Card}}s and performing actions
  3. Evaluation Phase -- Score objectives, pay {{glossary:upkeep|Upkeep}}, resolve end-of-Cycle effects

The number of Focus rounds per Cycle varies and is shown on the Galactic Event card revealed during Preparation. This means you will know exactly how many turns you have left in each Cycle to plan your actions.

callouts.content: With only 3 Cycles, every turn matters. Count the remaining Focus rounds on the Galactic Event card and plan your priorities accordingly.

title: Many Paths to Influence
textBlocks: {{glossary:influence|Influence}} flows from many different sources throughout the game. Understanding where Influence comes from helps you focus your strategy. Here are the primary sources:

Recurring sources (each Cycle during Evaluation):

  • {{glossary:agenda|Agenda}} Objectives -- Pure Agendas in your slots score Influence based on achievements and multipliers
  • Galactic Objectives -- The {{glossary:galactic_event|Galactic Event}} card provides goals everyone can pursue
  • {{glossary:upkeep|Upkeep}} penalties -- Lose 3 Influence per unpaid Upkeep (avoid this!)

During play:

  • Invading {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s -- Gain Influence from {{glossary:glory_token|Glory Token}}s when conquering Voidborn sectors
  • {{glossary:technology|Technology}} cards -- Each Technology gained provides an Influence bonus
  • {{glossary:overproduction|Overproduction}} -- If a resource production exceeds your {{glossary:stockpile|Stockpile}} cap of 15, gain 3 Influence per instance
  • {{glossary:civilization_track|Civilization Track}} advancement -- Various tiers grant Influence benefits
There is no single dominant path. The best players find synergies between economic production, military expansion, and objective completion.

callouts.content: Overproduction is easy to overlook but can be extremely powerful. Building a massive production engine that regularly exceeds the stockpile cap of 15 generates steady Influence income.

title: Sectors: The Building Blocks of the Galaxy
textBlocks:
The galaxy is made up of hexagonal tiles called {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s. Every sector on the map is in one of three control states:

  • {{glossary:voidborn|Voidborn}} sectors -- Controlled by the Voidborn. They contain Voidborn Fleets and {{glossary:corruption|Corruption}}. You must {{glossary:invade|Invade}} these to take them.
  • Player sectors -- Controlled by a player. They contain that player's {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}} (colored cubes). You build {{glossary:guild|Guild}}s and {{glossary:installation|Installation}}s here.
  • {{glossary:home_sector|Home Sector}} -- Your starting sector. Always under your control and can never be invaded by anyone.

Sectors that share a hex edge are adjacent. Adjacency is critical -- you can only {{glossary:regroup|Regroup}} fleet between adjacent sectors you control, and you can only {{glossary:invade|Invade}} sectors adjacent to ones you already hold.

callouts.content: Voidstorm tokens placed between sectors break adjacency. Two sectors separated by a Voidstorm are not considered adjacent, even if they share an edge. This can block your expansion routes.

rawHtml:
How Do You Score?

Sectors: The Building Blocks of the Galaxy

The galaxy is made up of hexagonal tiles called Sectors. Every sector on the map is in one of three control states:

  • Voidborn sectors -- Controlled by the Voidborn. They contain Voidborn Fleets and Corruption. You must Invade these to take them.
  • Player sectors -- Controlled by a player. They contain that player's Fleet Power (colored cubes). You build Guilds and Installations here.
  • Home Sector -- Your starting sector. Always under your control and can never be invaded by anyone.

Sectors that share a hex edge are adjacent. Adjacency is critical -- you can only Regroup fleet between adjacent sectors you control, and you can only Invade sectors adjacent to ones you already hold.

Voidstorm tokens placed between sectors break adjacency. Two sectors separated by a Voidstorm are not considered adjacent, even if they share an edge. This can block your expansion routes.

title: Pure vs Corrupted Sectors
textBlocks:
Sectors can be {{glossary:pure|Pure}} or {{glossary:corrupted|Corrupted}}:

  • Pure sectors have no Corruption marker. Their {{glossary:population|Population}} can be changed (increased or decreased) by game effects.
  • Corrupted sectors have a Corruption marker on them. Their Population is locked and cannot be changed.

When you conquer a Voidborn sector, it often starts Corrupted. Removing that Corruption is important for unlocking the sector's full potential.

title: Sector Infrastructure
rawHtml:
The Galaxy Map

Sector Infrastructure

Each sector has spaces for infrastructure and a Population value. Tap each element to learn more.

1 Population (1-6)

Most sectors have a Population value shown by a die. Population drives your resource production -- each Guild in a sector adds that sector's Population to the matching resource's Production Level. Higher Population means more resources.

2 Guild Spaces (up to 3)

Each sector has up to 3 spaces for Guilds. The 5 Guild types correspond to the 5 resources: Farmers (Food), Engineers (Energy), Miners (Materials), Bankers (Credits), Scientists (Science). Fill the leftmost empty space first.

3 Installation Spaces (up to 3)

Each sector has up to 3 spaces for Installations: Sector Defenses, Shipyards, and Starbases. These provide military infrastructure for deploying and defending fleets. Fill the leftmost empty space first.

4 Special Sector Abilities

Some sectors have unique abilities that trigger when you control them. These provide bonus effects beyond the standard Guild and Installation benefits. Check each sector's text when you claim it.

title: Five Resources
textBlocks:
Voidfall has 5 resources that fuel your empire:

  • Food -- Produced by Farmers {{glossary:guild|Guild}}s. Used to pay {{glossary:upkeep|Upkeep}} and for various actions.
  • Energy -- Produced by Engineers Guilds. Used for actions and can substitute for Food in Upkeep payment (combined with Materials).
  • Materials -- Produced by Miners Guilds. Used for building, fleet deployment, and Upkeep payment (combined with Energy).
  • Credits -- Produced by Bankers Guilds. A flexible resource that can substitute 1:1 for Food, Energy, or Materials when spending.
  • Science -- Produced by Scientists Guilds. Used for Technologies and advanced actions.

Each resource has a {{glossary:stockpile|Stockpile}} that caps at 15. You can never hold more than 15 of any single resource (but exceeding it triggers the valuable {{glossary:overproduction|Overproduction}} bonus of 3 {{glossary:influence|Influence}}).

callouts.content: Credits can substitute for Food, Energy, or Materials at a 1:1 rate when spending. However, Credits CANNOT substitute for Science or pay Upkeep. This makes Credits flexible but not universal.

title: How Production Works
textBlocks:
Resource production follows a logical chain:

  1. {{glossary:guild|Guild}}s generate {{glossary:production_level|Production Level}} -- Each Guild adds its {{glossary:sector|Sector}}'s {{glossary:population|Population}} to the matching resource's Production Level. Example: a Farmers Guild in a sector with Population 4 adds 4 to your Food Production Level.

  2. Production Level determines {{glossary:production_yield|Production Yield}} -- Your Production Level maps to a Yield value on your House mat's production track. The Yield is the actual amount of resources you gain. Most resources increase at a steady rate, but Credits increase more slowly.

  3. Yield adds to {{glossary:stockpile|Stockpile}} -- The resources go into your stockpile, capped at 15. Any excess triggers {{glossary:overproduction|Overproduction}} (3 Influence per instance).

The maximum Production Level is 13 per resource. Since Population ranges from 1-6 and you need multiple Guilds of the same type across different sectors to reach high levels, building a diverse empire with the right Guild placements is essential.

callouts.content: A sector with high Population and the right Guild type is extremely valuable. A Population 5 sector with a Farmers Guild contributes 5 to your Food Production Level from a single Guild placement.

Your Turn Begins: It is your turn within a Focus round.
Step 0: Reveal Crisis: Co-op/solo only. Draw a Crisis card if the current Alert is a Situation.
Step 1: Selection: Choose 1 Focus card from hand. Optionally flip a Trade token. Optionally play an Agenda card.
Step 2: Actions: Take up to 2 of the 3 Focus actions (or all 3 if you flipped a Trade token).
Step 3: Clean-up: Enforce fleet limits, limit Glory tokens to 4, place Agenda card, handle Trade tokens.
Step 4: The Void Advances: Co-op/solo only. Resolve Crisis effects (penalties, Catastrophes, or ongoing threats).
Turn Ends: Next player takes their turn.

title: Step 1: Selection
textBlocks:
At the start of your turn, you must choose 1 {{glossary:focus_card|Focus Card}} from your hand and play it face-up. This card determines which actions are available to you this turn.

You may also do two optional things during Selection:

  • Flip a {{glossary:trade_token|Trade Token}} -- This upgrades your turn from 2 actions to all 3 actions on the Focus card. You cannot flip a token you gained this same turn.
  • Play an {{glossary:agenda|Agenda}} card -- Place an Agenda from your hand alongside the Focus card. The Agenda type must match the Focus type.
rawHtml:
Your Turn

Step 1: Selection

At the start of your turn, you must choose 1 Focus Card from your hand and play it face-up. This card determines which actions are available to you this turn.

You may also do two optional things during Selection:

  • Flip a Trade Token -- This upgrades your turn from 2 actions to all 3 actions on the Focus card. You cannot flip a token you gained this same turn.
  • Play an Agenda card -- Place an Agenda from your hand alongside the Focus card. The Agenda type must match the Focus type.

title: Step 2: Actions
textBlocks:
Your Focus card shows 3 actions: Top, Middle, and Bottom. Normally you take 2 of the 3 actions (your choice). If you flipped a {{glossary:trade_token|Trade Token}} during Selection, you take all 3.

Each action has a cost (resources you must pay) and effects (what you gain or do). You must pay the cost before resolving the effects.

Within each action, effects are separated by colored lines:

  • Green line = resolve all effects shown (you get everything)
  • Red line = choose only one of the effects shown (pick the one you want)

In addition to Focus actions, you may also resolve your Agenda action (if you played one) and any Technology actions from your Technology cards.

callouts.content: Flipping a Trade token to get all 3 actions is extremely powerful. Save your Trade tokens for turns where all 3 actions on your Focus card are valuable to you.

title: Step 3: Clean-up
textBlocks:
After taking your actions, tidy up:

  • Fleet limits -- Each {{glossary:sector|Sector}} can have at most 2 {{glossary:fleet_token|Fleet Token}}s, each holding at most 3 {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}}. {{glossary:recall|Recall}} any excess back to your Active area.
  • {{glossary:glory_token|Glory Token}} limit -- You can hold at most 4 Glory tokens. Discard any excess.
  • Place {{glossary:agenda|Agenda}} -- If you played an Agenda this turn, place it in the appropriate slot on your House mat.
  • {{glossary:trade_token|Trade Token}}s -- Place gained Trade tokens on Agenda slots or return them to the Galactic board.

title: Fleet Power States
textBlocks:
Your military strength is represented by 14 {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}} cubes in your player color. These are the only player-colored components that go on the galaxy map (besides your {{glossary:home_sector|Home Sector}} Population die).

Fleet Power cubes exist in three states:

  • Inactive -- On your House mat in the Inactive area. These cubes are not yet available. You must activate them before they can be used.
  • Active -- On your House mat in the Active area. Ready to be deployed to the map.
  • Deployed -- On the galaxy map, placed on {{glossary:fleet_token|Fleet Token}}s in your {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s. This is your military presence.
rawHtml:
Your Turn

Fleet Power States

Your military strength is represented by 14 Fleet Power cubes in your player color. These are the only player-colored components that go on the galaxy map (besides your Home Sector Population die).

Fleet Power cubes exist in three states:

  • Inactive -- On your House mat in the Inactive area. These cubes are not yet available. You must activate them before they can be used.
  • Active -- On your House mat in the Active area. Ready to be deployed to the map.
  • Deployed -- On the galaxy map, placed on Fleet Tokens in your Sectors. This is your military presence.

title: Deploying Fleet Power
textBlocks:
To {{glossary:deploy|Deploy}} Fleet Power, you move cubes from your Active area to a sector on the map. When deploying, you choose a Fleet type and place cubes on a {{glossary:fleet_token|Fleet Token}} of that type.

Each sector can hold a maximum of 2 Fleet tokens, and each Fleet token holds 1-3 Fleet Power cubes. So the maximum military presence in a single sector is 6 Fleet Power (2 tokens with 3 cubes each).

To {{glossary:recall|Recall}} Fleet Power, you move cubes from the map back to your Active area. This happens when you take {{glossary:damage|Damage}} in {{glossary:combat|Combat}}, when you exceed fleet limits during Clean-up, or voluntarily.

callouts.content: You need a Shipyard or Starbase Installation in a sector to deploy Fleet Power there. Without one, you cannot place new Fleet tokens in that sector.

rawHtml:
Fleets and Fleet Power

Deploying Fleet Power

To Deploy Fleet Power, you move cubes from your Active area to a sector on the map. When deploying, you choose a Fleet type and place cubes on a Fleet Token of that type.

Each sector can hold a maximum of 2 Fleet tokens, and each Fleet token holds 1-3 Fleet Power cubes. So the maximum military presence in a single sector is 6 Fleet Power (2 tokens with 3 cubes each).

To Recall Fleet Power, you move cubes from the map back to your Active area. This happens when you take Damage in Combat, when you exceed fleet limits during Clean-up, or voluntarily.

You need a Shipyard or Starbase Installation in a sector to deploy Fleet Power there. Without one, you cannot place new Fleet tokens in that sector.

title: Regroup: Moving Between Your Sectors
textBlocks:
{{glossary:regroup|Regroup}} lets you redistribute your military across your territory. You can make up to 5 moves of {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}} between adjacent {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s you control.

Each move shifts one Fleet Power cube from one sector to an adjacent sector. You can move the same cube multiple times (spending multiple moves) or spread the moves across different cubes.
Critical restriction: You cannot move the last Fleet Power out of a non-Home sector. If you do, you would abandon that sector. Abandoning sectors is a separate action with its own consequences.

callouts.content: Use Regroup to concentrate your Fleet Power before launching an invasion. Five moves is enough to pull forces from across your territory to a front-line sector.

rawHtml:
Fleets and Fleet Power

Regroup: Moving Between Your Sectors

Regroup lets you redistribute your military across your territory. You can make up to 5 moves of Fleet Power between adjacent Sectors you control.

Each move shifts one Fleet Power cube from one sector to an adjacent sector. You can move the same cube multiple times (spending multiple moves) or spread the moves across different cubes.

Critical restriction: You cannot move the last Fleet Power out of a non-Home sector. If you do, you would abandon that sector. Abandoning sectors is a separate action with its own consequences.

Use Regroup to concentrate your Fleet Power before launching an invasion. Five moves is enough to pull forces from across your territory to a front-line sector.

title: Invade: Taking New Sectors
textBlocks:
To {{glossary:invade|Invade}}, you select a {{glossary:sector|Sector}} you do not control that is adjacent to one you do. Move {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}} from your adjacent sector(s) into the target, then resolve {{glossary:combat|Combat}}.

If you win the combat, you take control of the sector. If you lose, your Fleet Power is recalled and the sector remains under the defender's control.

Abandoning sectors: If you voluntarily leave a sector (move all Fleet Power out), that sector is abandoned. You must discard 1 {{glossary:glory_token|Glory Token}} per abandoned sector, and the {{glossary:voidborn|Voidborn}} takes control of it. Avoid this if possible -- it costs you Glory and gives territory back to the enemy.

callouts.content: Voidstorm tokens break adjacency. You cannot invade across a Voidstorm, even if the sectors share a hex edge. Plan your expansion routes around these obstacles.

title: Deterministic Combat
textBlocks:
{{glossary:combat|Combat}} in Voidfall is entirely deterministic -- there are no dice, no card draws, no randomness. You can calculate the exact outcome before committing to an invasion. This means combat rewards careful planning and math, not luck.

Combat has two sides: the Invader (the attacking player) and the Defender (whoever currently controls the sector -- either the {{glossary:voidborn|Voidborn}} or another player).

title: The Approach Step
textBlocks:
The {{glossary:approach|Approach}} is the first phase of combat. Before the main battle begins:

  • Each of the Defender's {{glossary:sector_defense|Sector Defense}}s deals 1 {{glossary:damage|Damage}} to the Invader
  • Each of the Defender's {{glossary:starbase|Starbase}}s deals 1 Damage to the Invader
  • Carriers on the Invader's side may deploy Corvettes (adding Fleet Power to the battle)

Approach Damage can only be cancelled by Approach {{glossary:absorption|Absorption}}. Regular Salvo Absorption does not help here.
rawHtml:

The Approach Step

The Approach is the first phase of combat. Before the main battle begins:

  • Each of the Defender's Sector Defenses deals 1 Damage to the Invader
  • Each of the Defender's Starbases deals 1 Damage to the Invader
  • Carriers on the Invader's side may deploy Corvettes (adding Fleet Power to the battle)

Approach Damage can only be cancelled by Approach Absorption. Regular Salvo Absorption does not help here.

title: Salvo Steps
textBlocks:
After the Approach, {{glossary:salvo|Salvo}} steps repeat until one side has no {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}} left:

  1. Calculate {{glossary:initiative|Initiative}} -- Each side gets 1 Initiative per Fleet Power in the combat sector, modified by Fleet types and {{glossary:technology|Technology}} bonuses
  2. Higher Initiative strikes -- The side with more Initiative deals 1 {{glossary:damage|Damage}} (opponent recalls 1 Fleet Power)
  3. Lower Initiative responds -- If they still have Initiative remaining, they deal 1 Damage back
  4. Equal Initiative -- Both sides deal 1 Damage simultaneously

Salvo Damage can be cancelled by Salvo {{glossary:absorption|Absorption}}. Some Fleet types and Technologies provide Absorption, which negates 1 point of Damage.

Combat continues until one (or both) sides run out of Fleet Power.

callouts.content: Since combat is deterministic, always calculate the outcome before invading. Count your Fleet Power and Initiative modifiers against the defender's. Never invade a sector you cannot win.

title: Who Wins the Battle?
textBlocks:
After {{glossary:combat|Combat}} resolves, there are three possible outcomes:

  • Defender victory -- The Defender still has {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}} remaining, the Invader does not. The sector stays under the Defender's control.
  • Invader victory -- The Invader has Fleet Power remaining, the Defender does not. The Invader takes control of the sector.
  • Combat tie -- Both sides have no Fleet Power remaining. The Defender discards a {{glossary:glory_token|Glory Token}}, and the sector is abandoned (no one controls it, the {{glossary:voidborn|Voidborn}} takes over).

title: After a Successful Invasion
textBlocks:
When the Invader wins:

  1. Remove {{glossary:installation|Installation}}s -- All Installations in the conquered sector are destroyed
  2. Resolve {{glossary:bounty_token|Bounty Token}}s and {{glossary:reclaim_token|Reclaim Token}}s -- Collect any special tokens in the sector
  3. Gain {{glossary:glory_token|Glory Token}} -- Take a Glory token from the supply
  4. Gain {{glossary:influence|Influence}} -- When invading a non-player sector (Voidborn), gain Influence equal to the sum of all your Glory token values

This means your first invasion might only gain you 1-2 Influence, but as you collect more Glory tokens, each subsequent invasion becomes more valuable. Building a collection of high-value Glory tokens makes every invasion increasingly rewarding.

callouts.content: Glory tokens have a snowball effect. Each new token increases the Influence you gain from future invasions. Prioritize invasions early to start building your Glory collection.

title: Voidborn vs Player Sector Invasions
rawHtml:
Invasion Outcomes

Voidborn vs Player Sector Invasions

The invasion rewards differ depending on whether you are conquering a Voidborn sector or another player's sector (competitive mode only).

1 Invading a Voidborn Sector

You gain a Glory Token and earn Influence equal to the sum of all your Glory token values. The sector may contain Bounty Tokens and Reclaim Tokens for additional rewards. The sector likely starts with Corruption that you will want to remove.

2 Invading a Player Sector (competitive only)

You gain Influence equal to the sum of the opponent's Glory token values (not yours). The opponent must discard one of their Glory tokens. This is a way to both gain Influence and weaken a rival's Glory collection simultaneously.

title: Technology Cards
textBlocks:
{{glossary:technology|Technology}} cards are powerful upgrades that enhance your capabilities. There are 84 Technology cards in the game: 56 Basic and 28 Improved.

Each Technology card provides three things:

  • {{glossary:influence|Influence}} bonus -- Gain Influence immediately when you acquire the Technology
  • Immediate effect -- A one-time benefit resolved when gained
  • Permanent ability -- An ongoing ability that lasts for the rest of the game

You have a limit of 5 Technologies at any time. This can increase to 6 by invading a Fallen House sector.

Technologies modify nearly every aspect of the game: they enable advanced Fleet types, enhance {{glossary:combat|Combat}} with {{glossary:initiative|Initiative}} and {{glossary:absorption|Absorption}} bonuses, improve resource {{glossary:production_level|Production Level}}s, and unlock powerful strategic options.

callouts.content: Technologies are how you specialize your Galactic House. A military-focused player might prioritize Fleet Technologies, while an economic player focuses on production enhancements. Choose Technologies that complement your overall strategy.

title: Basic vs Improved Technologies
textBlocks:
Basic Technologies can be acquired freely from the available tableau.

Improved Technologies are upgraded versions that require all three conditions:

  1. You already own the matching Basic version
  2. The Improved version is available on the Galactic board
  3. You have not exceeded your Improved Technology limit

Your Improved Technology limit is determined by your {{glossary:civilization_track|Civilization Track}} progress. Each track that reaches {{glossary:tier|Tier}} 1 unlocks 1 Improved Technology slot, and reaching Tier 2 on the same track unlocks another. So advancing all 3 tracks to Tier 2 gives you 6 Improved Technology slots.

title: Four Agenda Types
textBlocks:
{{glossary:agenda|Agenda}}s are strategic objective cards that drive your long-term planning. There are 4 types:

  • Support -- Objectives related to building and development
  • Might -- Objectives related to military power and conquest
  • Wealth -- Objectives related to economic production and resources
  • Dominance -- Objectives related to territorial control and expansion

You gain Agendas from the Agenda board's available offers. Some offers are {{glossary:corrupted|Corrupted}} -- taking them forces you to gain a {{glossary:corruption|Corruption}} marker along with the Agenda.

title: Playing and Placing Agendas
textBlocks:
The Agenda lifecycle has three stages:

  1. Gain -- Take an Agenda from the board offer during your actions
  2. Play -- During the Selection step of your turn, play an Agenda from your hand alongside a matching {{glossary:focus_card|Focus Card}} (the Agenda type must match the Focus type)
  3. Place -- During Clean-up, put the Agenda into one of your Agenda slots on your House mat (maximum 1 Agenda per type in play)

Evaluation scoring: During the Evaluation phase, each {{glossary:pure|Pure}} Agenda (without {{glossary:corruption|Corruption}} above it in its slot) is evaluated. Agendas have multiple sections with either achievements (exact rewards) or multipliers (per qualifying item). The benefit is always {{glossary:influence|Influence}}.

callouts.content: A Corrupted Agenda cannot score. If a Corruption marker sits above an Agenda in its slot, that Agenda is skipped during Evaluation. Keeping your Agenda slots pure is critical for scoring.

title: Three Tracks, Five Tiers
textBlocks:
Your Galactic House has 3 {{glossary:civilization_track|Civilization Track}}s representing different aspects of your civilization's development:

  • Society -- Cultural and social advancement
  • Statecraft -- Political and diplomatic development
  • Economy -- Industrial and financial growth

Each track has 5 {{glossary:tier|Tier}}s (0 through 4). You start at Tier 0 on all tracks and advance by spending the required costs during your actions.

Each Galactic House has unique benefits at each Tier on each track. This is one of the key asymmetric elements of Voidfall -- two players advancing the same track may unlock completely different abilities.

callouts.content: Read your House's track benefits carefully at the start of the game. They define your strengths and help guide your strategic direction.

title: Advancement Rules
textBlocks:
Advancing on {{glossary:civilization_track|Civilization Track}}s has important rules:

  • Tiers 1 and 2 -- Each unlocks 1 Improved {{glossary:technology|Technology}} slot. So reaching Tier 2 on all 3 tracks gives you 6 Improved Tech slots total.
  • Tiers 3 and 4 -- Before entering these tiers, you must deactivate {{glossary:fleet_power|Fleet Power}} (move cubes from Active back to Inactive). This represents the cost of pushing your civilization to its highest levels.
  • Tier 4 -- Required for building {{glossary:safe_haven|Safe Haven}} levels during Evaluation (important in cooperative/solo mode).

{{glossary:corrupted|Corrupted}} tracks: If a Corruption marker is on a Civilization track, you can still advance on it, but you do not gain the benefits of advancement until the Corruption is removed.

callouts.content: Deactivating Fleet Power for Tier 3-4 entry is a real cost. You temporarily weaken your military to advance your civilization. Time this carefully -- do not deactivate when you need those forces for defense.

title: How Corruption Works
textBlocks:
{{glossary:corruption|Corruption}} is the Voidborn's lasting mark on the galaxy. It is a persistent negative effect represented by markers placed on various parts of your game state. Corruption disables key functions:

  • Corrupted {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s -- Cannot change their {{glossary:population|Population}} value (locked in place)
  • Corrupted {{glossary:agenda|Agenda}} slots -- Agendas with Corruption above them cannot score {{glossary:influence|Influence}} during Evaluation
  • Corrupted {{glossary:civilization_track|Civilization Track}}s -- You can still advance, but you do not gain the tier benefits until Corruption is removed

How Corruption Works

Corruption is the Voidborn's lasting mark on the galaxy. It is a persistent negative effect represented by markers placed on various parts of your game state. Corruption disables key functions:

  • Corrupted Sectors -- Cannot change their Population value (locked in place)
  • Corrupted Agenda slots -- Agendas with Corruption above them cannot score Influence during Evaluation
  • Corrupted Civilization Tracks -- You can still advance, but you do not gain the tier benefits until Corruption is removed

title: Gaining, Moving, and Removing Corruption
textBlocks:
Gaining Corruption happens through several means:

  • Conquering Voidborn sectors (they often come with Corruption)
  • Taking {{glossary:corrupted|Corrupted}} Agenda offers from the board
  • Certain {{glossary:galactic_event|Galactic Event}} effects and {{glossary:crisis|Crisis}} penalties

Placement options when you must place a Corruption marker:

  • On a {{glossary:pure|Pure}} sector you control
  • On a non-starting Agenda slot
  • On a Civilization track marker

Removing Corruption is possible through various game effects -- certain Focus actions, Technology abilities, and other mechanisms allow you to discard Corruption markers. Prioritize removing Corruption from the locations where it hurts you most.

callouts.content: When forced to place Corruption, think carefully about where it hurts least. A Corrupted sector with low Population might be acceptable, while a Corrupted Agenda slot can cost you significant Influence every Evaluation.

title: Upkeep
textBlocks:
{{glossary:upkeep|Upkeep}} represents the maintenance cost of running your empire. Your total Upkeep is the sum of:

  • Upkeep icons on your placed {{glossary:agenda|Agenda}}s
  • Upkeep icons on occupied spaces in your {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s (Guild and Installation spaces that show Upkeep symbols)

To pay each point of Upkeep, spend 1 Food or a combination of Materials and Energy. Each point of Upkeep you fail to pay costs you 3 {{glossary:influence|Influence}}.
Important: Credits cannot pay Upkeep. Even though Credits substitute for Food/Energy/Materials in normal spending, Upkeep is an exception. You must use actual Food, Energy, or Materials.

callouts.content: Unpaid Upkeep at 3 Influence per point adds up fast. If you have 5 unpaid Upkeep, that is 15 Influence lost. Always plan your resource production to cover Upkeep before expanding further.

  • Multipliers -- Earn a reward for each qualifying item you have

{{glossary:agenda|Agenda}} Objectives work similarly but come from your placed Agendas. Only {{glossary:pure|Pure}} Agendas (without {{glossary:corruption|Corruption}} above them in their slot) are evaluated. The benefit from Agenda objectives is always {{glossary:influence|Influence}}.

title: Competitive End Game
textBlocks:
In competitive mode, the game ends after the Cycle 3 Evaluation phase. The player with the most {{glossary:influence|Influence}} wins.

Tiebreaker: If two or more players are tied on Influence, the player with fewer {{glossary:corruption|Corruption}} markers on their House mat and controlled {{glossary:sector|Sector}}s wins. A cleaner empire breaks the tie.

Your final Influence total reflects everything you accomplished across all 3 Cycles: Agenda scoring, Galactic objectives, invasion Glory, Technology bonuses, Overproduction, and minus any penalties from unpaid Upkeep or other losses.

callouts.content: In a close competitive game, Corruption markers become the tiebreaker. Removing Corruption is not just about unlocking benefits -- it can win you the game in a tie.

title: Cooperative / Solo End Game
textBlocks:
In cooperative and solo mode, you do not compete against each other. Instead, you calculate the {{glossary:voidborn|Voidborn}}'s total {{glossary:influence|Influence}} and every player must individually exceed that number to win.

The Voidborn's Influence starts at a base value determined by difficulty:

  • Easy: 60
  • Medium: 100
  • Hard: 140

Then additional penalties are added based on how much damage the Voidborn inflicted during the game.

  • Easy: 60
  • Medium: 100
  • Hard: 140

Then additional penalties are added based on how much damage the Voidborn inflicted during the game.

title: Voidborn Influence Breakdown
rawHtml:
End of Game Scoring

Voidborn Influence Breakdown

The Voidborn's final Influence is calculated by adding all of these sources to the base value. Tap each to see the details.

1 +30 per Rift

Each Rift on the map adds 30 to the Voidborn's Influence. Rifts represent major breaches in the galaxy's defenses.

2 +20 per incomplete Safe Haven

Each Safe Haven level that was not completed adds 20 to the Voidborn's total. Building Safe Havens requires reaching Tier 4 on Civilization Tracks.

3 +20 per Catastrophe

Each Catastrophe token adds 20. Catastrophes occur when Crisis cards are pushed off the Crisis board.

4 +10 per Harbinger on map

Each Harbinger still on the galaxy map adds 10. Clearing Harbingers reduces the Voidborn's score.

5 +5 per consumed Technology

Each Technology card consumed (removed from the game) by the Voidborn adds 5 to its total.

6 +5 per ongoing Crisis

Each unresolved Crisis still on the Crisis board at game end adds 5.

7 +3 per Fallen House card

Each Fallen House card (representing destroyed civilizations) adds 3 to the Voidborn's Influence.

8 +2 per Corruption anywhere

Every single Corruption marker in the game -- on sectors, Agenda slots, and Civilization Tracks -- adds 2 to the Voidborn's total.

9 +1 per Population in undefended Voidborn sectors

Each point of Population in Voidborn Sectors that do not contain any player Fleet Power adds 1 to the Voidborn's score.
